title: Medicine and technology
subtitle: pacemakers, prosthetic limbs, keyhole surgery
summary: Talk about the devices that medicine uses - from spectacles and crutches to robotic arms and keyhole surgery - and describe how fast the technology is advancing.

lesson.heading: A history of health technology
rows: **Spectacles**, probably invented by Arab scientists, were used to correct **vision**.
The first general **anaesthetic** was used in an operation in Japan.

lesson.heading: Words from that history
rows: a more formal word for glasses
something used to make you unconscious during an operation so that you feel no pain
a type of radiation that makes photographs of hidden objects such as bones possible
small pieces of transparent plastic worn on the eye to improve your sight
made in large numbers, usually in a factory
sticks that go under your arms to help you walk when you are injured

lesson.heading: The present day
lesson.text: Medical technology has made **rapid advances** in recent **decades**. Nowadays a **vast range** of **devices** is available.

examples.text: People with hearing difficulties wear **sophisticated hearing aids**.
examples.note: sophisticated = clever in a complicated way and able to do complicated tasks

examples.text: People with heart problems wear tiny **pacemakers**.
**Artificial** hips and knees are common, and are **highly efficient**.
examples.note: artificial = not natural, a copy made by humans; highly = very (more formal)

examples.text: People who have lost an arm or a leg can have a **prosthetic** leg or a modern **robotic** arm and hand.
Eyesight problems can be corrected by **laser surgery**.
examples.note: laser surgery = operations using powerful narrow beams of light

lesson.heading: Devices today
rows: a small device put inside the ear to help someone hear better
a small device put inside the chest to help the heart beat correctly
a man-made copy of the joint that connects the leg to the upper body
a leg made to replace a missing one
an arm that can be controlled and moved by the user
an instrument that measures someone's temperature
a machine that lets a doctor see inside someone's body

lesson.heading: Describing progress
lesson.text: These words and collocations are worth stealing whenever you write about technology of any kind.

examples.text: Medical technology has made **rapid advances** in the last **decade**.
examples.note: rapid = very fast; an advance = an improvement or development; a decade = a period of ten years

examples.text: There is now a **vast range of devices** that make life better for people with medical problems.
examples.note: vast = very wide; a device = an object or machine made for a particular purpose

lesson.heading: The future
lesson.text: A recent documentary predicted these developments in medical technology.

examples.text: **Scanners** which can **identify** health problems at an early **stage** will become more and more sophisticated.
examples.note: at an early stage = during the first period of development

examples.text: **Diagnosing** illnesses from a distance: patients will describe their symptoms and send information such as their **blood pressure** **automatically** to their doctor.
examples.note: diagnose = name the exact character of a disease by examining it

examples.text: Computers and huge **databases** will provide doctors with the **tools** to **treat** diseases.
**Keyhole surgery** will become more common: it will not be necessary to cut open a person's body to operate on them.
examples.note: keyhole surgery = operations in which a very small hole is made in the body to reach the organ inside

lesson.text: Doctors **operate on** a patient - the preposition is not optional. *Keyhole surgery means doctors no longer need to open a patient's body when they operate on them.*

pairs.right: to help someone with hearing difficulties
to help disabled people move around
to help an injured person to walk
to let a doctor see inside someone's body

exercises.prompt: *Glasses* is the everyday word; the more formal word is ___.
exercises.explanation: Spectacles, probably invented by Arab scientists, were used to correct vision.

exercises.prompt: Glasses were invented to correct difficulties with ___.
exercises.explanation: Vision is the ability to see.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: something that makes you unconscious during an operation
radiation used to photograph bones inside the body
a device that helps the heart beat correctly
made to replace a missing arm or leg

exercises.prompt: Medical scanners are ___ at this factory.
exercises.explanation: To manufacture is to make in large numbers, usually in a factory.

exercises.prompt: Medical technology has made rapid ___ in the last decade.
exercises.explanation: An advance is an improvement or development; *rapid advances* is a very common collocation.

exercises.prompt: There is now a ___ range of devices that make life better for people with medical problems.
exercises.explanation: *Vast* means very wide or very large.
*Highly* is a more formal alternative to *very* before adjectives like *efficient*.

exercises.prompt: Doctors will be able to identify diseases at an early ___ using sophisticated scanners.
exercises.explanation: *At an early stage* means during the first period of development.

exercises.prompt: Doctors will be able to ___ a patient's illness from a distance.
exercises.explanation: To diagnose an illness is to name its exact character by examining it.

exercises.prompt: Which sense or ability does each item help with?

options: Doctors no longer need to open a patient's body when they operate on them.
Doctors no longer need to open a patient's body when they operate them.
Doctors no longer need to open a patient's body when they operate at them.
Doctors no longer need to open a patient's body when they operate for them.
exercises.explanation: A surgeon always *operates on* a patient.

exercises.statement: In keyhole surgery the surgeon has to cut the patient's body wide open.
exercises.explanation: In keyhole surgery only a very small hole is made in the body to reach the organ or tissue inside.
